meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'well; come on', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'yes, indeed', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, that; it is', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'важительный'). Qualitative adjective formed with the productive suffix '-тельный'/'-ливый'. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('valid, respectful').

examples.text: Но у меня было уважительное оправдание.
examples.trans: But I had a valid excuse.

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'чина'). Common feminine noun meaning 'reason, cause' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Нет причин держать вас под арестом.
examples.trans: There is no reason to keep you under arrest.

examples.text: Нет причин держать вас под арестом. Сегодня вы выйдете отсюда.
examples.trans: There is no reason to keep you under arrest. Today you will walk out of here.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to want', paired with 'захотеть'.

examples.trans: If you don't want to, suit yourself.
They want to build a shopping centre there.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'висеть'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to depend on'.

related.gloss: not to to depend on (negated infinitive)

examples.text: Но всё зависит только от вас.
examples.trans: But everything depends only on you.

examples.text: Соберись, экономика города зависит от тебя.
examples.trans: Pull yourself together, the city economy depends on you.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'from; of', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'somebody, anyone', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Somebody on the street will tell him.

examples.text: Но здесь он всё равно узнает. Кто-нибудь на улице скажет.
examples.trans: But here he'll find out anyway. Somebody on the street will tell him.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'more', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: We need a more objective assessment.

examples.text: Погоди, нам нужна более объективная оценка.
examples.trans: Wait, we need a more objective opinion.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'woman' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Твоя жена очень мудрая женщина. Ты её слушай.
examples.trans: Your wife is a very wise woman. You listen to her.

meanings.note: Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'егда').

examples.trans: She's offended. She's always like that.

переезжать.gloss: to move (house), to relocate; to cross

meanings.en: to move (house), to relocate; to cross
meanings.note: Prefix 'пере-' denotes crossing over, repeating, or exceeding a limit (stem 'езжать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to move (house), to relocate; to cross', paired with 'переехать'.

examples.text: Ну и что? Я всё равно переезжать собираюсь.
examples.trans: So what? I'm planning to move anyway.

examples.text: Переезжай ко мне в большую квартиру.
examples.trans: Move in with me into a big apartment.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'to, towards', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: There's someone here to see you.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning '(emphasis) after all, but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

говорить.gloss: to speak, to say, to talk

meanings.en: to speak, to say, to talk
meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to speak, to say, to talk', paired with 'сказать'.
Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'чинить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to fix, repair', paired with 'чинить'.

examples.trans: I will try to fix it myself.
And can the state fix a tank?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ейчас').

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'крыть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to open', paired with 'открывать'.

examples.trans: Open the door. Is this flat nine?

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'chef' (head, leader, from Latin 'caput'); in Russian kitchen culture 'шеф' is the standard form of address for the executive head chef.

examples.trans: The chef is in the kitchen.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but; so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.
And does the governor support you?

examples.text: Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'добно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Шеф, а вам удобно сейчас говорить?
examples.trans: Chef, is this a convenient time for you to talk?

examples.text: На кухне все стараются работать удобно.
examples.trans: In the kitchen everyone tries to work comfortable.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything, all; that's it', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Мне всё равно. Что ты, что он.
examples.trans: It's all the same to me. You or him.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'he; it', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?
And this is for you. A toy car!

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'стить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to forgive; (imperative) excuse me', paired with 'прощать'.
High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'about', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'мнить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to remember'.

examples.trans: Do you remember the toilet in the communal flat?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'when', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: When I grow up, I'll be the mayor.

examples.text: Когда вырасту, ты будешь просить у меня прощения!
examples.trans: When I grow up, you'll be begging me to forgive you!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'with', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

поругаться.gloss: to quarrel, to have a fight

meanings.en: to quarrel, to have a fight
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'ругаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to quarrel, to have a fight', paired with 'ругаться'.

examples.trans: We will have a pretend quarrel in front of her.

examples.text: Нам нужно срочно поругаться перед ней.
examples.trans: We need to quarrel in front of her right away.

examples.text: Мы поругаемся понарошку, только для вида.
examples.trans: We will quarrel in pretend, only for show.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'option, variant, choice' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Пробуем, других вариантов у нас нет.
examples.trans: Let's try it, we have no other options.

examples.text: Это самый лучший вариант для всех.
examples.trans: This is the very best option for everyone.

examples.text: Трава, говорите? Отлично! Пробуем, других вариантов у нас нет.
examples.trans: Herbs, you say? Excellent! Let's try it, we have no other options.

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'брый'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('kind; good').

examples.text: Добрый вечер, Вика. С Новым годом!
examples.trans: Good evening, Vika. Happy New Year!

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'morning' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Какое хорошее утро! Лидия Алексеевна, чашку кофе, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: What a lovely morning! Lidia Alekseyevna, a cup of coffee, please.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'your', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?
Tell us, when will your programme be out?

meanings.note: Indeclinable neuter noun borrowed from French 'menu' (detailed list, from Latin 'minutus').

examples.text: Что за меню здесь? Как позвонить?
examples.trans: What's this menu here? How do I make a call?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to unbelievable'.

examples.trans: Vika, I am really hungry for something.
